The supabase function upsert point has the spaceId in its parameters, and should only allow upsert of local concepts. The eventual vercel upsert point should also have the spaceId in the path. Anyway, in the upsert/sync path, we're always bound by the current spaceId as given in the supabaseContext. If we need to go beyond that, we have the RID field which holds enough information to identify the space.

directMetadata: This is intentionally an implementation grab-bag to minimize database migrations; and the decision so far has been to make every defined property explicit in CrossApp, so that the CrossApp does not need to know about this database implementation idiosyncrasy. So I think we should not add it to CrossApp. (I have it in crossAppSchemaBase, and that may have been a mistake.)

Anything we need to put there has to be explicitly added to CrossApp: This obviously applies to format and colour.

Another case that is important: Obsidian stores node instance frontmatter in the `source_data` variable. We need to expose that separately.

Obsidian also stores `label`, which... may have been needed to handle the name collision issue you raise? To be reviewed.

Name: May be worth using the full path minus the path of the discourse graph folder. Will resolve to just the name in many cases, but not when it matters. Does not need separate storage.

importedFromRid: imported instances are not re-exported, but schemas are. May be worth adding to DB for that reason. (May even be worth a column.) BUT I think it requires deeper design. An imported schema may be the synthesis of many imported schemas from different spaces. (See [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/IM2y99NZO](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/IM2y99NZO>) and [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/w8k2RA1C0](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/w8k2RA1C0>) for details.) Do we pick one, many? I have an intuition it may be tied to the design for collaborative documents, actually. In any case, no urgency to put it in the database.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-23T17:55:46.952Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-23T17:55:46.916Z","parentId":"769132d9-f7a0-48e7-8ef3-a3adc81c92d3","resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"f1207324-84ec-4684-b3be-3d153fffefc9","name":"Marc-Antoine Parent"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"769132d9-f7a0-48e7-8ef3-a3adc81c92d3","body":"Decision: the ticket's Solution and Done When settle it. Discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, and `SharedNode` is removed. Sid agreed on 2026-10-22. His 2026-07-20 point about a light listing still holds: `content.full` is optional, and import fetches the full content on its own.

- Fields to add: every field a caller reads from the listing today, as the Solution says.
  - `spaceId` in `CrossAppBase` (Michael, 2026-08-07), plus `spaceName`, `platform` and `directMetadata`.
  - Also read today, and missed in the first version of this comment: `spaceUri` (Roam shows and filters on it; `rid` carries it but is optional), the node type's database id (Roam resolves node types by it in `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`), and the author's database account id (Obsidian's import modal shows author names from it).
  - `modifiedAt` has to stay the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content, as `lastModified` is today, or refresh misses edits to a node's body.
  - The rest already exists in another form: `localId`, `content.direct.value`, the dates and `slots`.
- "sourceId": answered in this ticket as "Equivalent to sourceLocalId", which already maps to `localId`. Nothing to add.
- ENG-1985 builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter for nodes, and this ticket uses it.
- ENG-2045 follows this ticket.

Open, needs Marc-Antoine: for the three missed fields, add each to `CrossAppNode`, or change its caller to the CrossApp form (a required `rid`, node types resolved by local id, author names looked up by local id).","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-22T05:53:56.737Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-22T06:37:44.721Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"b35b996b-7f48-4bdb-b75f-90d6005cf8b8","name":"siddharth yadav"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}

content.content: @AGENTS.md

You are working on the Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Roam Style Guide

Platform-native UI - use BlueprintJS 3 components and Tailwind CSS.
Use `text-red-700` for error message text so errors have a consistent visual treatment. Keep danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, and diagram colors separate from this text convention. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`.
Do not introduce arbitrary visual styling, new shading colors, background palettes, gradients, accent colors, border colors, or text colors unless the user explicitly asks for them.
When styling Roam UI, use this priority order:

1. Use basic BlueprintJS patterns and components first.
2. Reuse existing repo examples and established Tailwind styling patterns before adding anything new.
3. Fall back to Roam-native styling and colors.

Any new Roam UI should feel native to Roam and consistent with existing BlueprintJS and repository usage, not like a separate visual palette.
Use the roamAlphaApi docs from https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/tIaOPdXCj.
Use Roam Depot/Extension API docs from https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/y31lhjIqU.

{"comments":[{"id":"ad9d794f-8968-415f-bfb1-8358f6ab9f6f","body":"Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): `CrossAppNode` follows the pattern of the other CrossApp types and gains no space or listing fields. This replaces the field list in the 2026-10-22 Decision comment and the Solution's "Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes", after Marc-Antoine's -1 (2026-10-23).

The schema and relation converters already work this way. Each object carries a `rid`, local ids and the author's local id. Roam relation discovery looks spaces up separately with `getSpaceMap` (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:81`).

Each field a caller reads from `SharedNode` today moves like this:

- `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`: discovery returns the spaces next to the nodes. A caller finds a node's space from the space in its `rid`. The converter sets `rid` on every node.
- `schemaId`: callers resolve the node type by the schema's rid (the node's space and `nodeType`), as relation discovery does with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
- `authorId`: `CrossAppNode.authorId` is the author's account local id. Callers look names up by it.
- `directMetadata`: dropped. Its only reader is Obsidian import, for `filePath`, and import reads `filePath` again with each node's content (`importNodes.ts:1767-1774`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`).
- `title`, `created`, `lastModified`: `content.direct.value`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`. `modifiedAt` stays the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content.

`importedFromRid` stays as it is today: a field Obsidian keeps locally on imported notes, node types and relations. Discovery doesn't read it. Storing it in the database (one source space or several for a schema) is a later design question, not part of this ticket.

PRs, in order:

1. ENG-1985 adds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter.
2. This ticket's first PR: discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and the spaces, and the Roam callers switch.
3. ENG-2045: Obsidian import switches.
4. This ticket's last PR: delete `SharedNode`.

The supabase function upsert point has the spaceId in its parameters, and should only allow upsert of local concepts. The eventual vercel upsert point should also have the spaceId in the path. Anyway, in the upsert/sync path, we're always bound by the current spaceId as given in the supabaseContext. If we need to go beyond that, we have the RID field which holds enough information to identify the space.

directMetadata: This is intentionally an implementation grab-bag to minimize database migrations; and the decision so far has been to make every defined property explicit in CrossApp, so that the CrossApp does not need to know about this database implementation idiosyncrasy. So I think we should not add it to CrossApp. (I have it in crossAppSchemaBase, and that may have been a mistake.)

Anything we need to put there has to be explicitly added to CrossApp: This obviously applies to format and colour.

Another case that is important: Obsidian stores node instance frontmatter in the `source_data` variable. We need to expose that separately.

Obsidian also stores `label`, which... may have been needed to handle the name collision issue you raise? To be reviewed.

Name: May be worth using the full path minus the path of the discourse graph folder. Will resolve to just the name in many cases, but not when it matters. Does not need separate storage.

importedFromRid: imported instances are not re-exported, but schemas are. May be worth adding to DB for that reason. (May even be worth a column.) BUT I think it requires deeper design. An imported schema may be the synthesis of many imported schemas from different spaces. (See [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/IM2y99NZO](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/IM2y99NZO>) and [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/w8k2RA1C0](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/w8k2RA1C0>) for details.) Do we pick one, many? I have an intuition it may be tied to the design for collaborative documents, actually. His 2026-07-20 point about a light listing still holds: `content.full` is optional, and import fetches the full content on its own.

  - `spaceId` in `CrossAppBase` (Michael, 2026-08-07), plus `spaceName`, `platform` and `directMetadata`.
  - Also read today, and missed in the first version of this comment: `spaceUri` (Roam shows and filters on it; `rid` carries it but is optional), the node type's database id (Roam resolves node types by it in `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`), and the author's database account id (Obsidian's import modal shows author names from it).

content.content: @AGENTS.md

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible
- The plugin ships with `isDesktopOnly: false`, so it must load on mobile
- Node builtins and `electron` are deliberately not in the esbuild `external` array in `scripts/compile.ts`. Marking them external lets a dependency's `require("fs")` reach the bundle and throw on mobile; leaving them out fails the build instead. Replace the dependency rather than re-adding the external

### Code quality

- Use `const`/`let` — never `var`
- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

## Unit tests

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Put tests in `src/**/__tests__/<module>.test.ts`, next to the code they cover. Tests covering the test scaffolding itself live in `test/`; those two globs are the whole of `include` in `vitest.config.mts`.
- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.
- `obsidian` ships type declarations with no runtime entry point, so `vitest.config.mts` aliases it to `test/obsidianStub.ts`. Add to that stub whatever a new test needs to load its module; use `vi.mock("obsidian")` in the test itself when the test needs to assert on a call.
- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Obsidian ships its implementation in `obsidian.asar`, in the resources directory of the installed app, and the current cases were settled by reading it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Put tests in `src/**/__tests__/<module>.test.ts`, next to the code they cover. Tests covering the test scaffolding itself live in `test/`; those two globs are the whole of `include` in `vitest.config.mts`.
- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.
- `obsidian` ships type declarations with no runtime entry point, so `vitest.config.mts` aliases it to `test/obsidianStub.ts`. Add to that stub whatever a new test needs to load its module; use `vi.mock("obsidian")` in the test itself when the test needs to assert on a call.
- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Obsidian ships its implementation in `obsidian.asar`, in the resources directory of the installed app, and the current cases were settled by reading it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

name: Database tests
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "packages/database/**"
env:
  SUPABASE_USE_DB: local
  SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: test
  GITHUB_TEST: test

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 10.15.1
          run_install: false
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "pnpm"
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # - name: Get supabase version
      #   working-directory: ./packages/database
      #   run: echo "SUPABASE_VERSION=$(./node_modules/.bin/supabase --version)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      # - name: Cache Docker images.
      #   uses: AndreKurait/docker-cache@0.6.0
      #   with:
      #     key: docker-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.SUPABASE_VERSION }}
      - name: Setup database
        working-directory: ./packages/database
        run: pnpm run setup
      - name: Serve and run tests
        working-directory: ./packages/database
        run: pnpm run test:withserve

name: Database tests
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "packages/database/**"
env:
  SUPABASE_USE_DB: local
  SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: test
  GITHUB_TEST: test

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 10.15.1
          run_install: false
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "pnpm"
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # - name: Get supabase version
      #   working-directory: ./packages/database
      #   run: echo "SUPABASE_VERSION=$(./node_modules/.bin/supabase --version)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      # - name: Cache Docker images.
      #   uses: AndreKurait/docker-cache@0.6.0
      #   with:
      #     key: docker-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.SUPABASE_VERSION }}
      - name: Setup database
        working-directory: ./packages/database
        run: pnpm run setup
      - name: Serve and run tests
        working-directory: ./packages/database
        run: pnpm run test:withserve

Since the schema's format happens to match the expected title, this fallback masks a potential regression, meaning the format field is load-bearing in a way that weakens what the test actually guards against.

Weighing whether to keep or delete the format field: it mirrors real Roam behavior where nodeSchemaToCrossApp always sends format, so it's realistic fixture data. But without format, the fallback would just return the full title and fail to match coreTitle, meaning the test would actually catch a core_title regression that it currently can't.

That's a minor masking issue but not a true finding, since the fallback path is designed for nodes lacking core_title and discovery still correctly returns the published coreTitle either way — so I'll log it as considered and cleared rather than flag it as a fix.

Now I'm looking at the space URL lookup: it's constructed from the space name and read back via the service client for verification. I'm weighing whether to hoist a shared helper that derives the URL directly versus reading it from the database, since reading from the DB more honestly reflects what discovery actually keys on.

This confirms it's a low-medium severity finding — I'd fix it by hoisting a small helper function that builds the Roam space URL from a space name, then reusing it at both call sites instead of doing a separate service-client lookup, which trims out roughly ten unnecessary lines. **Mode: Full.** This is the first pass. The branch isn't pushed, there's no PR, no bot comments and no earlier pre-pr-review run. Change set: `git diff eng-2091-remove-sharednode...HEAD`, 1 commit (402fc510), 3 files, +133/-11. I ignored the uncommitted `supabase/config.toml` as instructed.

The example contract is now correct, and every local check passes. There is one Medium test-design finding and two Low wording findings.

## 1. Findings (by severity)

**F1 (Medium): the round trip reads through Roam's refresh lookup, not the discovery path both imports use.**
- **Where:** `packages/database/features/step-definitions/stepdefs.ts:978-994`
- **What:** the Then step calls `getSharedNodeByRid`. Its only production caller is Roam refresh (`apps/roam/src/utils/refreshImportedNode.ts:81`). Discovery in this codebase is `listGroupSharedNodes`, which both import paths call (`apps/roam/src/utils/discoverSharedNodes.ts:20`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/ImportNodesModal.tsx:75`).
- **Second lookup:** to build the rid it looks up, the step reads `Space.url` with the service-role client, which bypasses RLS. That URL was already built from the space name at `stepdefs.ts:239`. This fails check 1h.
- **Why it matters:** both paths share `dbNodesToCrossApp`, so the conversion is covered either way. The listing's own queries (`sharedNodes.ts:106-121`) are not covered, and neither is the space resolution import relies on. The step also does a privileged read the real reader never does. The ticket says "read back through discovery".
- **Fix:** replace lines 978-994 with the listing, and import `listGroupSharedNodes` and `getSharedNodeSpace` instead of `getSharedNodeByRid`:
  ```ts
  const client = await getLoggedinDatabase(readerSpaceId);
  const { nodes, spaces } = await listGroupSharedNodes({ client, currentSpaceId: readerSpaceId });
  assert.equal(nodes.length, 1);
  const [node] = nodes;
  assert.ok(node);
  const space = getSharedNodeSpace({ node, spaces });
  assert.equal(space.id, publisherSpaceId);
  const published = roamOriginNodeExample;
  ```
  In the expected object, set `rid: spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid(space.url, published.localId, "note")`.
  - `getServiceClient` and the `publisherSpace` query go away.
  - `assert.ok(node)` is needed because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on.
  - The `my_contents` read at 1017-1024 then follows Roam import exactly: listing, `getSharedNodeSpace` (`importSharedNodes.ts:113`), then `fetchFullMarkdown(space.id, node.localId)` (`materializeSharedNode.ts:219-226`).
  - The commit message names `getSharedNodeByRid`, so update it too.
  - If the author keeps `getSharedNodeByRid`, at least build the URL from the `:239` template (hoisted to a helper) instead of the service-client read, and annotate why refresh stands in for discovery.

**F2 (Low): the acceptance criterion says `full` reads back through discovery, but discovery returns no `full`.**
- **Where:** `packages/database/features/sharedNodeRoundTrip.feature:8-9`
- **Why it matters:** discovery selects only `last_modified, source_local_id, space_id` for `full` (`sharedNodes.ts:37`), per ENG-2091's 2026-10-25 Decision. The step reads `full` from `my_contents`. A reader of this criterion would assume discovery carries the body, which is the #1214 "listing fetches summaries" lesson in reverse.
- **Fix:** "* The example Roam node, written with the shared converters, reads back through discovery with the same direct content, node type and source identity, and its full content row holds the published body and content type".
- **Optional nit, line 5:** the "So that" states a developer goal. The existing features phrase it from the user's side, e.g. "So that what I import from another space is what that space published".

**F3 (Low): the user name in the feature has to match the example's `authorId`, and nothing says so.**
- **Where:** `sharedNodeRoundTrip.feature:13,22` and `crossAppNodeContract.example.ts:51`
- **What:** the example's `authorId: "maparent"`. The upsert resolves authors by `PlatformAccount.account_local_id` (`content.sql:428-430`), so the Background must open a user called `maparent`.
- **Why it matters:** rename that user and, by my trace (not run), the author goes unresolved. Either the publish assert at `stepdefs.ts:961` fails as `[-N]` vs `[]`, or discovery skips the node with "Missing author". Neither points at the cause.
- **Fix:** draft annotation A6 below. A one-line Gherkin `#` comment on line 13 would also work, but sid's no-inline-comments rule argues for the annotation.

**Considered and cleared**
- **`format` on the inline schema (`stepdefs.ts:952`):** this scenario only reaches it through discovery's fallback when `core_title` is null (`dbToCrossAppConverters.ts:349-350`), and it never is null here. It stays because it's what Roam writes for a Claim (`defaultDiscourseNodes.ts:8`; `nodeSchemaToCrossApp` always sends `format`). It would hide a `core_title` write regression, but users would still see the same `coreTitle`, so "reads back as published" holds.
- **`?.` at 962 and 1027-1028:** the types force them. `data` is `number[] | null` because `assert.equal` doesn't narrow, and `full` is optional on `CrossAppNode`. If either value is missing, the `deepEqual` fails, so neither hides a failure.

## 2. Verification log
- **Mode gate:** no PR, no annotations, no earlier SHA, so Full.
- **Step 0:** DATA files are the example, `stepdefs.ts` (`.rpc`/`.from`) and the `.feature`. No FRONTEND files. The base stack changes nothing under `packages/database/supabase` relative to main (`git diff --stat` is empty), so CI's migrations-only setup matches.
- **1a Reuse:**
  - New things: two steps and one feature. No inline literal unions.
  - The existing `user {word} upserts these concepts to space {word}:` step (`:734`) takes raw JSON and has no negative-id check, so the new step is justified: it has to go through the shared converters.
  - No existing discovery step.
  - No full-content read helper exists in `packages/database/src`. The test's query matches Roam's app-local `fetchFullMarkdown` column for column.
- **1b Justification:** only `|| {}` on `world.localRefs` (the existing pattern) and `format` (cleared above). Nothing to delete.
- **1c Literals:** `"note"` appears once in the diff and matches 3 existing call sites; `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid` ignores the subtype for `https://` URLs. Clean.
- **1d Type honesty:** `as LocalRefsType` is the file-wide pattern. No `!` or `any`. The three `?.` are justified. Clean.
- **1e Explainability:** every hunk maps to a Done When item or to the ts-node import fix. Clean.
- **1f Call graph:** no new exports or parameters. `roamOriginNodeExample` has two consumers, `rewriteAssetLinks.test.ts` (passes) and `stepdefs`. Clean.
- **1g Comments:** zero comment lines added. Clean.
- **1h Second lookup:** the `Space.url` service read fails this check (F1). The `my_contents` full read is required, because discovery omits `full` by decision.
- **1i Workflow injection:** no workflow changes, so n/a.
- **2a Invariants walk:**
  - `is_relation`, `is_schema`: apply only inside lib, and are satisfied.
  - Timestamps: lib appends `Z` (`normalizeUtcTimestamp`), the writer uses `toISOString`, and the test compares `Date`s. Satisfied.
  - Generated types: n/a.
  - Push predicates down: satisfied.
  - Pagination, per-item loop: n/a.
  - Listing payload: satisfied.
  - RLS empty-result: n/a.
  - `original = true` with `maybeSingle`: satisfied at `:1023`.
  - RID-only identity: satisfied.
  - direct/full disjoint, `full` optional: satisfied.
  - Contracts in `crossAppContracts`: n/a.
  - Boundary validation, content-model transforms, frontmatter, platform from RID, format precedence: n/a.
  - Converter matrix: no field added.
  - Sync gating: n/a (test-only write).
  - Datalog, telemetry, migrations: n/a.
  - Unresolved reference fails the row: the node's schema reference resolves because `upsert_concepts` loops in order (`concept.sql:478`) and the schema comes first. The negative-id assert guards this.
  - `upsert_content` is PUT: n/a.
  - `getConcepts nodeIds`: n/a.
  - Empty table cell: n/a, the only table is SpaceAccess with no empty cells.
- **2b Provenance:**
  - `Space.url` (text) feeds the rid.
  - `my_contents.text` and `content_type` are compared by equality.
  - No timestamp is parsed in the diff. Clean.
- **2c Query review:** `Space` by id with `.single()` is unique. The full read filters `space_id`, `source_local_id`, `variant` and `original`, then `maybeSingle()`. No query in a loop. Clean.
- **2d Contract check:** no new or changed contract types.
- **2e Example vs Roam converter, field by field:**
  - `localId`, `nodeType` match.
  - `coreTitle` matches: it equals `extractContentFromTitle("[[CLM]] - {content}", title)`.
  - `direct` `{localId, value: full title}` matches `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:87-90` and `:145-148`.
  - `full` `{localId, value, contentType: roamMarkdown, scale: "document"}` matches `:66-71`.
  - The body is the `buildFullMarkdown`/`toMarkdown` output for 4 top-level bullet blocks: a `- ` prefix per block, joined with `\n`, one trailing `\n`.
  - `[[EVD]]` survives because `simplifiedFilename` and `removeSpecialCharacters` are false.
  - `{{[[pdf]]: …}}` isn't matched by `EMBED_REGEX`.
  - `slots` is absent, as it should be.
  - Content-level `authorId` was dropped, which matches the converter.
  - The one remaining divergence is `assets`, which the converter never sets. It stays because rewriteAssetLinks reads it (A3).
- **2f Flag-gated writes:** no production write paths.
- **Step 3 (frontend):** skipped, no FRONTEND files.
- **Step 4 (process):**
  - Scope: clean.
  - Size: 133+/11-, mostly test.
  - Bots: none.
  - Chain: covers Roam-origin only. Obsidian-origin is deferred to ENG-1986 and must be named in the PR.
  - No guard removals, and no parity table needed.
  - Runtime proof: the cucumber suite runs in CI on PRs touching `packages/database/**` (`test-database.yaml`, Node 22). No demo needed.
  - Breadcrumbs: needed, see the annotations.
- **Commands:**
  - `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`: `packages/database` exit 0, `apps/roam` exit 0. The database tsconfig includes `features/step-definitions`.
  - `vitest run`: database 143/143 tests (11 files). Roam 710/710 (75 files), including rewriteAssetLinks' "the cross-app contract fixtures round-trip".
  - `eslint --max-warnings 0` on the two `.ts` files: 3 warnings, all unused-disable directives at `stepdefs.ts:81`, `:92` and `:843`. `git blame` puts them in 43b82a8fd (Marc-Antoine, 2026-05-21). Added lines are 16-22 and 937-1031, so none carries a warning.
  - `prettier --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
  - Under ts-node: root `@repo/content-model` fails with `Cannot find module './adapters/index.js'`, while `/constants`, the example, `lib/sharedNodes`, `lib/crossAppConverters` and `lib/rid` all load. `crossAppContracts.ts:1` already imports from the `/constants` subpath. The author's claim holds.
  - I did not run cucumber, per the brief.
- **Commit:** author sid597, no Co-Authored-By (it has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer).
